letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: Sounds like the 'o' in British English 'hot' or 'not' — a rounded, open back vowel, not like the English 'a' in 'cat'.

letters.name: á
letters.memoryTrick: A long 'a' sound, like the 'a' in English 'father' but held longer — the accent mark lengthens the vowel.

letters.name: bé
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'b' in 'ball' — a simple voiced bilabial stop. Easy to remember: just like 'b' in any language.

letters.name: cé
letters.memoryTrick: Always pronounced like 'ts' in 'cats' — never like 'k' or 's' alone. Think of the 'ts' at the end of 'hats'.

letters.name: csé
letters.memoryTrick: Just like English 'ch' in 'church' or 'chocolate'. The 'cs' digraph is one of the most common in Hungarian — think of it as one letter.

letters.name: dé
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'd' in 'dog' — a straightforward voiced dental stop, simpler than English because it's always clear, never softened.

letters.name: dzé
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ds' in English 'beds' or 'kids' — a voiced version of 'c' (ts). Rare at the start of words, more common in the middle.

letters.name: dzsé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'j' in 'jazz' or 'jungle' — the 'd' + 'zs' combination makes the same sound. It appears mostly in loanwords.

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'e' in English 'bet' or 'red' — an open mid-front vowel. Never silent, never like the English 'ee' sound.

letters.name: é
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ay' in English 'say' or the 'e' in Spanish 'qué', but held longer — a long, clean mid-front vowel. The accent signals length.

letters.name: ef
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'f' in 'fire' — a simple voiceless labiodental fricative, exactly as you would expect.

letters.name: gé
letters.memoryTrick: Always hard like 'g' in English 'go' or 'game' — never soft like 'g' in 'gem'. Hungarian 'g' is always a voiced velar stop.

letters.name: gyé
letters.memoryTrick: A voiced palatal stop — try saying 'd' with your tongue pressed to the roof of your mouth, like the 'd' in British 'due' or 'duke'. Not like 'g' + 'y' separately.

letters.name: há
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'h' in 'house', but Hungarian 'h' is always pronounced — never silent, even at the end of words like 'méh' (bee).

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ee' in English 'see' but SHORT — tighter and shorter. The long version is 'í' with an accent. Hungarian keeps vowel length distinct.

letters.name: í
letters.memoryTrick: A LONG 'ee' like in English 'see' or 'tree' — the accent mark means you hold this vowel for roughly twice as long as the unaccented 'i'.

letters.name: jé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'y' in 'yes' or 'yellow' — Hungarian 'j' is a y-sound, never like the English 'j' in 'jam'. The letter 'ly' makes the same sound.

letters.name: ká
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'k' in 'key' or 'kitten' — a voiceless velar stop, always hard and clear. Hungarian doesn't have silent 'k' like English 'knee'.

letters.name: el
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'l' in 'love' — but Hungarian 'l' is always a clear, front-of-the-mouth 'l', never the dark 'l' of English 'milk'.

letters.name: ely
letters.memoryTrick: Pronounced exactly like Hungarian 'j' (English 'y' in 'yes'). Historically it was a palatal 'l' like Spanish 'll', but today it sounds the same as 'j'. You just have to memorize which words use 'ly' and which use 'j'.

letters.name: em
letters.memoryTrick: Same as English 'm' in 'mother' — a simple bilabial nasal, identical across most languages.

letters.name: en
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'n' in 'nose' — a simple alveolar nasal. Never silent, always pronounced clearly in every position.

letters.name: eny
letters.memoryTrick: Like Spanish 'ñ' in 'señor' or the 'ny' in English 'canyon' — a palatal nasal, made by pressing the tongue to the roof of the mouth. Think 'ny' = 'ñ'.

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'o' in English 'or' but shorter and tighter — a mid-back rounded vowel. Keep it crisp, not drawn out like the English 'oh'.

letters.name: ó
letters.memoryTrick: A LONG 'o' like in English 'go' or 'so' — hold the rounded lip position about twice as long as short 'o'. The accent means duration.

letters.name: ö
letters.memoryTrick: Like the German 'ö' or the 'eu' in French 'peur' — round your lips as if saying 'o' but say 'e' instead. Short and crisp, not drawn out.

letters.name: ő
letters.memoryTrick: The LONG version of 'ö' — hold the rounded front-vowel position twice as long. The double accent on 'ő' means both front-rounded AND long. Unique to Hungarian.

letters.name: pé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'p' in 'pen' — a voiceless bilabial stop. Hungarian 'p' is never aspirated strongly like English 'p' at the start of words.

letters.name: kú
letters.memoryTrick: Only used in loanwords and foreign names — pronounced like 'k'. It appears in the Hungarian alphabet for foreign words but native Hungarian words never use it.

letters.name: er
letters.memoryTrick: A rolled or tapped 'r' like in Spanish or Italian — made by fluttering the tip of the tongue against the ridge behind the teeth. Never like the English throaty 'r'.

letters.name: es
letters.memoryTrick: This is the tricky one: Hungarian 's' sounds like English 'sh' in 'shoe'! For the normal 's' sound, Hungarian uses 'sz'. Think: Hungarian 's' = 'sh', Hungarian 'sz' = 's'.

letters.name: esz
letters.memoryTrick: This is the NORMAL 's' sound, like English 's' in 'sun'. Counterintuitive: Hungarian 's' alone = 'sh', but 'sz' together = plain 's'. Think 'SZ' = 'Simple S'.

letters.name: té
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 't' in 'top' but with less aspiration — keep it clean and unaspirated, like the 't' in Spanish or French. Your tongue touches further forward than in English.

letters.name: tyé
letters.memoryTrick: A voiceless palatal stop — like saying 't' with your tongue pressed to the roof of your mouth, similar to the 't' in British 'tune'. The voiceless twin of 'gy'.

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'oo' in English 'book' or 'foot' but a bit tenser — a short, rounded high back vowel. Not drawn out like English 'oo' in 'moon' — that's the long 'ú'.

letters.name: ú
letters.memoryTrick: A LONG 'oo' like in English 'moon' or 'soon' — hold the rounded lip position about twice as long as short 'u'. The accent means you extend the sound.

letters.name: ü
letters.memoryTrick: Like German 'ü' or French 'u' in 'tu' — round your lips as if saying 'oo' but say 'ee' instead. Short and crisp. The long version is 'ű'.

letters.name: ű
letters.memoryTrick: The LONG version of 'ü' — hold the front-rounded lip position twice as long. The double accent on 'ű' means both front AND long. Unique to Hungarian.

letters.name: vé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'v' in 'voice' — a voiced labiodental fricative. Simple and consistent, never silent.

letters.name: dupla vé
letters.memoryTrick: Only used in loanwords and foreign names — pronounced like Hungarian 'v'. The name 'dupla vé' means 'double v'. Native Hungarian words never contain 'w'.

letters.name: iksz
letters.memoryTrick: Only in loanwords and international terms — pronounced like 'ks'. The letter name 'iksz' reflects its sound. It appears in words like 'taxi' and 'expressz'.

letters.name: ipszilon
letters.memoryTrick: As a standalone letter, only in loanwords and old family names — pronounced like Hungarian 'i'. The letter name 'ipszilon' comes from Greek. In modern Hungarian digraphs (gy, ly, ny, ty) it's part of one sound.

letters.name: zé
letters.memoryTrick: Like English 'z' in 'zebra' or 'buzz' — a voiced alveolar fricative. Always clearly voiced, not like the German 'z' (which is /ts/ — that's Hungarian 'c').

letters.name: zsé
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 's' in English 'pleasure' or 'measure', or the 'j' in French 'je' — a voiced 'sh' sound. Think of the 'zh' buzz in 'treasure'.
